content: The purpose of creating microchapters is to achieve several specific goals. These include reducing the amount of content on any single page to ensure faster page loading times, enabling users to navigate to their desired content more quickly, lowering the barrier to entry for younger contributors by allowing them to focus on a manageable scope of content, and issuing microcredits for Continuing Medical Education (CME). To automate the creation and cataloging of microchapters, the titles of these chapters should only capitalize the first letter of the first word. For example, Pericarditis Causes should be written as Pericarditis causes. A navigation box template can be found on the right-hand side of the page under How to create an expanded navigation box. This navigation box is a template placed at the top of the page. To set it up, search for the placeholder text type page name here and replace it with the name of the disease or chapter. Do not replace the term PAGENAME. Save the navigation box template as Template: Type page name here. When editing and creating microchapters, certain elements should be removed. Replace the WikiDoc Cardiology Network Infobox template with the template specific to the disease being worked on. The structure of the disease's homepage should align with the navigation box. Additionally, improve the English language as needed. The structure of microchapters is as follows: 1. Overview: This section should provide a concise description of the key aspects of the condition, with a focus on its diagnosis and treatment. Content from copyleft government sites can serve as a guide. This section should link to more detailed microchapters. 2. Patient Information: Use copyleft patient information from government sites like the NHLBI or NLM. This information should be written at an 8th-grade reading level. Ensure the link to the WikiDoc page is placed at the top. 3. Pathophysiology: This section should describe the biological mechanisms underlying the disease, including embryological or developmental abnormalities, molecular abnormalities, genetic abnormalities, and pathology images. 4. Demographics and Epidemiology: This microchapter should discuss the incidence and prevalence of the disease in both developed and developing countries. 5. Screening: This section should include screening procedures for the disease. It is rarely included in the navigation box. 6. Natural History, Complications, and Prognosis: This microchapter should describe the natural progression of the disease if left untreated, its complications, and the prognosis. 7. Causes: This section should list all conditions that cause the disease, as well as conditions associated with the disorder but not causative. It should not describe what the disease causes (this belongs in the Natural History and Complications chapter) or how to distinguish the disorder from others (this belongs in the next chapter). 8. Differentiating the Disease from Other Disorders: This microchapter should describe findings that distinguish the disease from others with similar symptoms, including physical examination findings and laboratory results. Organizing distinguishing features systematically can be helpful. 9. History and Symptoms: This section should describe the typical symptoms reported by patients. It should not include physical examination findings (signs of the disease). Organizing symptoms by frequency is recommended. 10. Physical Examination: This section should describe the signs of the disease observed during a physical examination. Symptoms should not be included here. Findings can be organized as follows: appearance of the patient, vital signs, skin, eyes, ears, nose, throat, heart, lungs, abdomen, extremities, and neurologic findings. 11. Laboratory Tests: This section should include information about laboratory tests such as electrolytes (e.g., potassium, sodium), kidney function (e.g., creatinine, BUN), liver function tests (e.g., SGOT, SGPT), complete blood count (e.g., WBC, hematocrit, hemoglobin), etc. It should not include imaging study results (e.g., chest X-ray, CT, MRI) or pathology images, which belong in the Pathophysiology section. 12. Imaging Studies: This section should cover imaging and other diagnostic studies. 13. Treatment: This section does not link to anything. Only Medical Treatment and Surgery link to chapters. 14. Medical Treatment: This section should describe the drugs used to treat the condition, including their dosage and duration of therapy. It should also include guidance on when to escalate therapy or manage treatment failures. 15. Surgery: This section should include the indications for the procedure, a description of pre-operative tests, the surgery itself, and post-operative care. 16. Primary Prevention: This microchapter should describe therapies used to prevent the first occurrence of the disease. 17. Secondary Prevention: This microchapter should describe therapies used to prevent a second occurrence or recurrence of the disease.
